newsitem.title: USA: Western U.S. spot power slips on weather, natgas.
newsitem.headline: Western U.S. spot power slips on weather, natgas.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the western U.S. slipped Monday, pressured lower by an outlook for milder weather in the region and tumbling natural gas values across the country.

January gas prices at major U.S. western receipt points declined in tandem with the Gulf Coast market. January natgas delivered to the San Juan/Blanco Hub was quoted near $2.90 per million British thermal units.
The latest 11-15 day forecasts showed the West would enjoy normal to above-normal temperatures.

Above-normal amounts of rain and snow in the Pacific Northwest for the rest of the week could boost the amount of water available for hydroelectric generation in coming weeks, brokers and traders said.
Bonneville Power Adminstration (BPA) today cut its daily offers of off-peak power in the Northwest.

BPA lowered light-load deliveries Tuesday to $21.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) in the Northwest and the California-Oregon Border (COB), compared with next-day offers at $22.25 for the Northwest and $23.00 for COB.

The start of a 70-day refueling shutdown at 1,070 megawatt (MW) San Onofre nuclear power unit 2 Saturday was offset by news of the 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon unit 1 returning to full output, brokers and marketers noted.
Firm, peak COB electricity for Tuesday was assessed at $29.25-$29.75 a megawatt hour (MWh), compared with Friday's $29.00-31.00.
Firm, off-peak COB power for Tuesday held steady at $17.00-$18.00.

COB deliveries for the balance of December were pegged at $28.00-$29.50, a wider range than Friday's notational $28.00-29.00. January COB was last quoted at $24.00-$24.50, down from $25.25-$25.50 Friday.
First-quarter 1997 COB fell near $20.30, down from Friday's $21.50-22.00.
Next-day firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was discussed near $28.75-$29.25, compared with Friday's notational range of $28.00-30.00 for Monday.
Tuesday firm, off-peak Mid-C values stayed notionally at $14.00-17.00.
Mid-C power for the rest of December was valued at $27.75-$28.75, compared with Friday's notational $27.50-28.50. January Mid-C deliveries were talked at $23.00-$24.00.
First-quarter 1997 Mid-C electricity was quoted at $19.60-$20.00.
In the Southwest, Palo Verde (PV) next-day power for firm, peak delivery was discussed near $25.75-$26.25, compared with Friday's $25.00-$27.00.
Firm, off-peak PV power for Tuesday delivery remained in the $13.00-$14.00 range.
"There a little early morning heating demand (in the Southwest)," said a New York broker.
Balance-of-December PV power slid near $27.50, down from Friday's $28.00-29.00. January 1997 PV deliveries were talked at $24.00-$24.75, lower than $25.50-26.50 Friday.
First-quarter 1997 PV power fell to $21.50-$22.00, down from Friday's $22.00-22.75.
Four Corners firm, peak power for Tuesday delivery was assessed near $27.00 with offers as high as $30.00, comparing with Friday's notational $25.50-26.50.
Firm, next-day, off-peak power at Four Corners was offered as high as $17.00, compared with $14.00-$17.00 Friday.
--R Leong, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1622
